original_value: WiFi indoor personnel behavior recognition has become the core technology of wireless network perception. However, the existing human behavior recognition methods have great challenges in terms of detection accuracy, intrusion, and complexity of operations. In this paper, we firstly analyze and summarize the existing human motion recognition schemes, and due to the existence of the problems in them, we propose a noninvasive, highly robust complex human motion recognition scheme based on Channel State Information (CSI), that is, CSI-HC, and the traditional Chinese martial art XingYiQuan is verified as a complex motion background. CSI-HC is divided into two phases: offline and online. In the offline phase, the human motion data are collected on the commercial Atheros NIC and a powerful denoising method is constructed by using the Butterworth low-pass filter and wavelet function to filter the outliers in the motion data. Then, through Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM) training and classification, we establish offline fingerprint information. In the online phase, SoftMax regression is used to correct the RBM classification to process the motion data collected in real time and the processed real-time data are matched with the offline fingerprint information. On this basis, the recognition of a complex human motion is realized. Finally, through repeated experiments in three classical indoor scenes, the parameter setting and user diversity affecting the accuracy of motion recognition are analyzed and the robustness of CSI-HC is detected. In addition, the performance of the proposed method is compared with that of the existing motion recognition methods. The experimental results show that the average motion recognition rate of CSI-HC in three classic indoor scenes reaches 85.4%, in terms of motion complexity and indoor recognition accuracy. Compared with other algorithms, it has higher stability and robustness.

result.paraphrase: WiFi-based indoor personnel behavior recognition has become a key technology for wireless network sensing. However, existing human behavior recognition methods face major challenges in detection accuracy, intrusion, and operational complexity. In this paper, we first analyze and summarize current human motion recognition schemes, and in view of their problems, we propose a noninvasive, highly robust CSI-based complex human motion recognition scheme, CSI-HC, using the traditional Chinese martial art XingYiQuan as the complex-motion background for verification. CSI-HC consists of two phases: offline and online. In the offline phase, human motion data are collected with a commercial Atheros NIC, and a robust denoising method is built using a Butterworth low-pass filter and wavelet functions to remove outliers from the motion data. Then, through Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM) training and classification, offline fingerprint information is established. In the online phase, SoftMax regression is used to correct the RBM classification, process motion data collected in real time, and match the processed data with the offline fingerprint information. Based on this, complex human motion recognition is achieved. Finally, repeated experiments in three classic indoor scenes are used to analyze the parameter settings and user diversity that affect motion recognition accuracy and to evaluate the robustness of CSI-HC. In addition, the proposed method is compared with existing motion recognition methods. Experimental results show that the average motion recognition rate of CSI-HC in three classic indoor scenes reaches 85.4%, and it performs better in motion complexity and indoor recognition accuracy. Compared with other algorithms, it offers higher stability and robustness.
